Apple Podcasts is my go-to podcast app, but for years the core "Up Next" queue feature has had a number of problems. The good news is that iOS 27.2 finally brings a fix.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' "Up Next" queue into two sections: "New Episodes" and "Continue Listening"

Apple Podcasts has a lot going for it. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my go-to. I've also loved all the recent video-related upgrades.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core "Up Next" queue has had me tempted to switch to other apps.

I've written before about why the "Up Next" feature is frustrating to use. Here's a quick recap:

  • It's hard to see at a glance which podcasts are available to listen to
  • Sometimes episodes can easily disappear, even if you're halfway through listening

However, I'm excited to say that iOS 27.2 brings a long-overdue fix for "Up Next." The solution is to split the feature into two separate sections:

  • New Episodes
  • Continue Listening

At the very top of the app is "New Episodes," which looks much like the old "Up Next" and works in largely the same way. As the name suggests, it only shows you the latest episode of every show you follow.

"Continue Listening" sits right below it as a dedicated area where you can see all the episodes you've started but not yet finished.

Together, these two sections address all of my biggest complaints about the old "Up Next" queue.

At a glance, it's easy to see what's new to listen to, and there's no longer any fear of losing episodes, because everything you've started can be found in "Continue Listening." There are still some minor issues left unaddressed, but these changes alone resolve my main problems with "Up Next."

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is a great time to give it another go.

Do you use Apple or another podcast app? Let us know in the comments.
